A road bridge about 2 kilometres long joining Malé, the crowded capital island of the Maldives, to Hulhulé, the airport island, and on to the new reclaimed island of Hulhumalé. It opened on 30 August 2018 and was the first bridge between islands in the country.

Before it, people crossed by ferry. Malé is one of the most densely built cities in the world, and the bridge was meant to let people and business spread to Hulhumalé. It was built by a Chinese state company and paid for mostly by Chinese grants and loans, during the government of Abdulla Yameen, which tilted the Maldives toward China. Its original name was the China-Maldives Friendship Bridge.

It became a symbol of the Belt and Road Initiative in South Asia and of the contest between China and India for influence in the Indian Ocean. Critics in the Maldives worried about debt to China, and governments since have shifted back and forth between the two powers. The islands had long been a crossroads of sea trade, since before the Maldives turned to Islam in the 12th century.
